issues.legal_issue: A conditional gift of immovable property does not become complete where acceptance is unproved and the donor retains possession and enjoyment during life, and the donor may cancel it before death while it remains incomplete.
material_facts: The donor executed a registered deed describing the transfer as conditional and limiting the donee’s rights until the donor’s death.
The deed reserved to the donor possession of the property and the right to let rooms and collect their rents during the donor’s lifetime.
The deed contained no recital of acceptance, and there was no evidence proving acceptance by the donee.
The donor executed a cancellation deed before death, stating that possession had not been handed over and that the conditional gift was cancelled.
After the cancellation, the donor executed a will in favour of the appellant and another beneficiary.
issues.conclusion: The gift did not become complete during the donor’s lifetime and was ineffective and inoperative; it was duly cancelled. The appeal was allowed and the suit claiming title under the gift was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 122 and 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, a gift requires acceptance by or on behalf of the donee during the donor’s lifetime and, as the court explained, execution of the registered gift deed, acceptance, and delivery of the property together complete the gift. The court read the deed as a whole, harmonising its clauses to give effect to the parties’ manifested intention. Because acceptance was unproved and the donor retained possession and enjoyment under a conditional, limited transfer, the gift had not become complete and could be cancelled before the donor’s death. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_title_decree and donee_acceptance_not_proved and donor_retained_lifetime_possession_and_enjoyment and gift_rights_limited_until_donor_death and donor_executed_cancellation_before_death

predicates.appeal_from_title_decree: A party appealed a decree in a suit seeking a declaration of title based on a disputed gift.
predicates.donee_acceptance_not_proved: The donee’s acceptance of the gift was not established by the deed or other evidence.
predicates.donor_retained_lifetime_possession_and_e: The donor retained possession and the right to enjoy the property during the donor’s lifetime.
predicates.gift_rights_limited_until_donor_death: The gift deed limited the donee’s rights until the donor’s death.
predicates.donor_executed_cancellation_before_death: The donor executed a deed cancelling the gift before the donor died.

issues.definition: When a title appeal concerns a conditional gift that was not accepted, left the donor in possession and enjoyment for life, and was cancelled by the donor before death, the gift is treated as inoperative and effectively cancelled.
